title: How often the Cancer Drug List is updated and how Singapore keeps pace with international cancer care
asked: Dr Hamid Razak asked how frequently the Cancer Drug List (CDL) is reviewed and updated, and what measures reduce the risk of Singapore lagging behind prevailing international standards of cancer care.
response: The CDL lets MOH negotiate better drug prices, and since it began, cancer drug prices have fallen by an average of 30%, and up to 60% for some drugs. MOH updates the CDL three times a year with an expert committee of public and private sector cancer specialists, taking into account medical advancements, clinical and cost-effectiveness evidence and alignment with international standards. 400 drug-indication pairings have been listed, comparable to all pairings approved in 2022 before the CDL. Patients needing drugs not yet listed can seek financial assistance case-by-case through MediFund.

key_points.point: Cancer drug prices have dropped by an average of 30%, and up to 60% for some drugs, since the CDL was implemented.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we have managed to reduce cancer drug prices by an average of 30%, and up to 60% for some drugs

key_points.point: The CDL is updated three times a year, in consultation with an expert committee of cancer specialists from the public and private sectors.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: MOH updates the CDL three times a year, in consultation with an expert committee comprising cancer specialists from public and private sectors

key_points.point: 400 drug-indication pairings have been listed, comparable to all pairings approved in 2022 before the CDL.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: we have listed 400 drug-indication pairings, which is comparable to all the pairings approved in 2022, before CDL was implemented

key_points.point: Patients who need cancer drugs not yet on the CDL can get financial assistance in public healthcare institutions case-by-case through MediFund.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: there are avenues for financial assistance in public healthcare institutions on a case-by-case basis through MediFund

key_points.point: The Agency for Care Effectiveness does horizon scanning to track drugs approved overseas and engages companies to encourage submissions.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: the Agency for Care Effectiveness (ACE) conducts horizon scanning to track approved drugs overseas and proactively identify priority drugs

key_points.point: Clinicians may submit requests directly to ACE to evaluate treatments for possible inclusion in the CDL.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: the clinicians may directly submit requests to ACE to evaluate treatments for potential inclusion in the CDL

key_points.point: Direct clinician submissions are intended largely for very rare cancers, where there are fewer than five to 10 patients a year and the treatment is not Health Sciences Authority-registered but has been approved by at least one overseas reference regulator.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: where there are fewer than five to 10 patients per year where the treatment is not Health Sciences Authority-registered due to the very small patient numbers

key_points.point: On clinicians' administrative burden from insurers' forms and pre-approvals, the Minister said it could be taken separately to see how best to streamline the processes.
key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: We could take that separately and we could see how best we could streamline those processes.

left_open: Whether Shield providers and insurers will stop requiring pre-approvals and forms for drugs already on the CDL, which the Minister said would be taken separately.
Whether the number of drugs approved overseas but not on the CDL is tracked and reported.
supplementary: Whether overseas-approved drugs missing from the CDL are tracked, how clinicians can request evaluation, and insurer administrative burdens.
